methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target distributed skill-building outside traditional tech hubs, creating peer learning pathways that could democratize deep capability rather than just tool adoption.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents organized regional capacity-building in a non-metro area, signaling potential for distributed depth if evaluation translates to sustained training infrastructure rather than one-off platform deployment.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon canceling four NoVA data centers due to backlash reveals infrastructure concentration without community integration—economic development that neither deepens local capability nor distributes benefits, leaving regions competing for contested facilities.

signals.title: Rural advocacy groups band together to oppose data centers, related energy projects
signals.signal_reading: Rural coalitions opposing data centers signal extraction without capability transfer—infrastructure arrives but generates neither local AI fluency nor meaningful economic participation, concentrating costs while exporting value.

signals.title: ODU, CHKD want to map hotspots of childhood asthma in Hampton Roads with AI - WHRO
signals.signal_reading: ODU-CHKD partnership using AI for asthma mapping demonstrates deep institutional capability in Hampton Roads health tech sector, but research application doesn't necessarily signal workforce distribution or broad community AI literacy.
